correctness.rationale: Literal simplicial deletion-link cone identity, skeleton acyclic-toggle lemma, (r-2)-connectivity of n-fold join for n>=2 and nullhomotopic link embedding produce actual homotopy cofiber splitting. Integral exterior-chain contraction and equivariant long exact sequence prove both natural Z-modules, including graded block-swap signs. Two independent complete face/boundary and signed-Lefschetz finite checker methods corroborate nontrivial cases; all-parameter theorem is supported by the general proof, not extrapolated from finite checks.

evidence: arxiv:2001.06775 Theorem 16 gives wedge-of-spheres for chordal higher independence, not multiplicities.
arxiv:2505.06614 Corollary 3.3 and Theorem 4.7 prove shellability for the same star-clique/small-diameter block family, but not exact ranks or integral automorphism modules.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Known broader qualitative theorems DO subsume connectivity/shellability/wedge existence, and those statements are excluded from novelty. Their conclusions do not imply the exact 2-grade binomial multiplicities or exterior-power module actions, which are the specific new assertions.

evidence: Trees in arxiv:2605.25150 have no clique triangles and cannot instantiate nontrivial bouquets.
The broad shellability and chordal wedge results establish only qualitative properties, not the two independent exact ranks or natural signed Z-lattices.
Topological join and skeleton lemmas are treated as prior tools, not new claims.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The precise conclusion is a canonical family-wise integral homotopy type and equivariant integral homology module with explicit two-degree multiplicities. It is a strict quantitative/equivariant refinement of broader shellability, not a restatement or corollary containing only the already-known qualitative conclusion.

evidence: Star-clique graph terminology defined in arxiv:2505.06614 Section 3, notably Corollary 3.3.
The higher-independence connected-component definition coincides with the forbidden induced connected (r+1)-vertex hypergraph formulation in arxiv:2505.06614 Section 1.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Star-clique, windmill, block clique bouquet, and connected-component forbidden-hypergraph formulations were compared. The same family has a known shellability result but not the exact two-degree integral homotopy and symmetry claim.

evidence: arxiv:2001.05448 classifies complete multipartite, cycle and other graph families rather than one-cut-vertex clique bouquets.
The primary star-clique paper arxiv:2505.06614 contains no exact Betti table or exterior-power formula for these bouquets.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Checked potential face-count-only equivalence, exact numerical tables, and general generating-family statements. A face-count formula at one small independence parameter is weaker than integral homotopy and signed symmetry for arbitrary r>=3. No dominating exact table was found; absence is not a proof of novelty.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge comparison of complete accessible primary sources finds broader general chordal and same-star-clique shellability established, but no two-degree binomial-rank complete integral homotopy theorem with signed exterior-power symmetry modules for arbitrary r>=3 and unequal clique blades. Existing broad qualitative statements explicitly acknowledged; residual unindexed overlap is not ruled out.
residual_risks: An unindexed, inaccessible or differently named star-clique homotopy computation might coincide with the quantitative part.
The complete all-parameter signed integral module description was not found in sources inspected; further specialist review is desirable.

value.rationale: Natural connected chordal block-graph family with arbitrary r>=3 and unequal clique sizes has uniform exact integral mixed-dimensional sphere wedge ranks, explaining two independent topological sources of homology. Integral graded block-symmetry modules further refine known general star-clique shellability. Cases with both low and high ranks nonzero exhibit meaningful mixed-dimensional behavior; this is not a merely routine one-graph enumeration or textbook qualitative restatement.
